claim.pdf_says: 14.9.28.3   Syntax rules — a fourth-level clause heading, set in the same style and at the same level as 14.9.28.1 General and 14.9.28.2 General formats on page 712.
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect class as page 674: the siblings on page 712 are `### 14.9.28.1 General` and `### 14.9.28.2 General formats`, so `##` here breaks the section tree and detaches the PERFORM syntax rules from the PERFORM statement. `## 14.9.28.4 General rules` (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29212) carries the same error.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The claim is filed as kind=missing-heading, but the heading is present verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29150 — `## 14.9.28.3 Syntax rules` — preceded at line 29146 by the correct anchor ``. The claim itself quotes the markdown containing the heading it calls missing. I also compared the full body of the rendered page against the transcription: 'where times-phrase is:', 'where until-phrase is:', 'where varying-phrase is:' with all three syntax diagrams, then 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' and syntax rules 1) through 4) with sub-items a), b), c) — every word is present and correct. No spec text, rule number, or clause number differs. (2) The PDF has no heading levels to lose. I rendered both pages at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs. On p712 the printed headings '14.9.28 PERFORM statement', '14.9.28.1 General' and '14.9.28.2 General formats' are set in the IDENTICAL typeface, weight, size and left margin — there is no typographic distinction between the third-level and the fourth-level clause at all. '14.9.28.3 Syntax rules' on p713 is set in that same single heading style. The claim's premise, that the PDF sets 14.9.28.3 'at the same level as' .1 and .2 and therefore markdown must mirror that with `###`, describes a distinction the printed page does not make: the PDF conveys hierarchy solely through the dotted clause number, and the markdown reproduces that number exactly. Markdown hash depth is an authoring artifact with no PDF counterpart, i.e. formatting, which is an explicit rejection criterion. (3) The claimed harm does not follow from the claimed cause. The headings in this neighbourhood are, in order: line 29041 `## Page 712`, 29043 `# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)` (the running header, as an H1), 29046 `## 14.9.28 PERFORM statement`, 29049 `### 14.9.28.1 General`, 29054 `### 14.9.28.2 General formats`, 29105 `## Page 713`, 29150 `## 14.9.28.3 Syntax rules`, 29173 `## Page 714`, 29212 `## 14.9.28.4 General rules`. Any outline built from hash depth is already partitioned by the `## Page NNN` markers sitting at the same level 2 as the clause headings, and reset entirely by the level-1 running header. Promoting line 29150 to `###` would nest it under `## Page 713`, NOT under `## 14.9.28 PERFORM statement` — so the proposed fix cannot produce the attachment the claim says it restores. The hierarchy that actually resolves 14.9.28.3 is the dotted number and the `section-14-9-28-3` anchor, and both are correct. (4) It is not a page-713 phenomenon. The pattern is systemic across the whole transcription: 620 four-component headings use `###`, 162 use `##`, 24 use `####`; three-component headings split 508/276/17 the same way; five-component split 128/118/41. Within 14.9 alone the same 'defect' appears at 14.9.1.3, 14.9.1.4, 14.9.2.3, 14.9.2.4, 14.9.4.3, 14.9.10.4, 14.9.11.4, 14.9.12.4, 14.9.13.3, 14.9.13.4, 14.9.14.3, 14.9.14.4 and beyond — and 14.9.1.1/14.9.1.2 are `####` while their own siblings 14.9.1.3/14.9.1.4 are `##`, so 'match the siblings' has no stable target. Hash depth in this file tracks per-page conversion noise, not clause depth. Filing one instance as a page-713 PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy mislabels a global markdown-normalization chore as a spec-fidelity defect. No semantics of the PERFORM statement, and no citable rule, are affected. If the project wants a uniform outline it is a single global pass over heading depth (and over the page/running-header markers, which are the larger problem), not a per-page reconciliation finding.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. The heading '14.9.28.3 Syntax rules' is present verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29150 with the correct `section-14-9-28-3` anchor, and every word of page 713 is faithfully transcribed. The only difference is markdown hash depth (`##` vs `###`), which has no counterpart in the PDF — the printed standard sets 14.9.28, 14.9.28.1, 14.9.28.2 and 14.9.28.3 in one identical bold style and conveys level only through the dotted number, which the markdown preserves. The claimed harm is also unfounded: `## Page 713` (line 29105) sits between the PERFORM heading and its syntax rules at the same level 2, and a level-1 running header at 29043 resets the tree, so promoting 29150 to `###` would attach it to the page marker rather than to the PERFORM statement. The inconsistency is systemic (162 four-component headings at `##` vs 620 at `###`, including 14.9.1.1/.2 at `####` next to 14.9.1.3/.4 at `##`) and belongs in a one-time global heading-normalization pass, not in the per-page spec reconciliation ledger.
